name: Ransomware Pre-Deployment Simulation
description: Simulate the four-phase ransomware pre-deployment sequence: disable backup services, narrate shadow copy deletion, stage a ransom note and encrypted file markers, then generate the Sophos XDR detection handoff. Designed to show how MDR interrupts a ransomware attack before any files are actually encrypted.

prelude.title: {{customerName}} — Live Attack Chain
prelude.subtitle: A realistic multi-stage ransomware storyline built to show stakeholders exactly how a high-consequence attack unfolds, why it matters to {{customerName}}, and how Sophos surfaces the incident inside Central before impact becomes business reality.
prelude.transitionLine: Now let’s move into Sophos Central and show how this incident becomes visible to your team in real time.
expectedDetections: VSS and WBEngine service disabled by non-system process
vssadmin or wmic shadowcopy delete command execution
High-confidence ransomware precursor — automatic MDR escalation

mitreTechniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

slides.title: Initial compromise at {{customerName}}
slides.body: A user opens a convincing business file and triggers a ransomware chain. What looks like a single bad click quickly becomes an enterprise risk event for {{customerName}}.

slides.title: The attacker moves toward impact
slides.body: Before encryption begins, the attacker weakens recovery by disabling protections, targeting shadow copies, and staging the conditions for business disruption.

slides.title: Sophos changes the outcome
slides.body: Sophos surfaces the precursor behavior, escalates the threat, and gives the team at {{customerName}} a response path before encryption becomes business reality.

talkingPoints: Ransomware operators spend weeks inside a network before they encrypt anything — they're maximizing blast radius
Shadow copy deletion is the single highest-confidence ransomware signal — when we see it, we escalate immediately
Sophos MDR stops ransomware at the pre-deployment phase — before a single file is encrypted

healthcare: Healthcare ransomware directly impacts patient care — hospitals have diverted ambulances and cancelled surgeries after attacks
The average healthcare ransomware attack costs $1.4M and takes 54 days to recover from — MDR prevention is orders of magnitude cheaper
HIPAA breach notification requirements mean every encrypted patient record is a reportable incident
financial_services: The average ransomware demand in financial services is now $4.7M — and that's before regulatory fines and reputational damage
Wire transfer fraud and ransomware are increasingly combined — attackers encrypt and extort simultaneously
MDR's 24/7 coverage means we catch ransomware at 3am on a Sunday — when your team isn't watching
manufacturing: Ransomware on OT systems stops production lines — the cost per hour of downtime often exceeds the ransom demand itself
Manufacturing is the #1 targeted sector for ransomware — attackers know operational disruption creates payment pressure
MDR catches the IT foothold before attackers ever reach OT systems

runbookSteps: Frame it: 'This is the scenario your prospect fears most. Let's show them exactly how we stop it.'
Launch simulation — walk through each phase as it executes
Phase 1 (defense disable): 'This is the attacker preparing the battlefield — removing your recovery options'
Phase 2 (shadow copies): 'This is the point of no return in most ransomware attacks — we catch it here'
Phase 3 (ransom note): 'Show the actual ransom note file in File Explorer on the Windows VM — very visual'
Switch to Sophos XDR: show the critical alerts firing, analyst escalation workflow, isolation recommendation
clickPath: Start on the alert view and show the critical ransomware-related precursor activity that would immediately draw analyst attention.
Open the investigation or case context to show how Sophos connects the activity into a coherent incident, not just isolated alerts.
Move into detections and threat activity to prove the attack chain, then close on the response outcome and why the attack did not become a business crisis.
